title: Reading a calcium trace
objective: Interpret a calcium-imaging experiment including its controls.

steps.title: Responders and a final check
steps.body: A calcium experiment ends by asking: which neurons responded to each stimulus, and are the quiet ones actually alive? A high-**KCl** pulse at the end depolarizes *every* healthy neuron — a positive control that a non-responder was silent, not dead.

visual.alt: Five cultured DRG neurons expressing GCaMP, each with a ΔF/F trace. Capsaicin brightens only the two TRPV1-positive neurons. KCl then brightens every healthy neuron. One neuron responds to neither, so it is excluded as unhealthy.
visual.caption: Capsaicin finds the responders; KCl checks the quiet ones are alive.

steps.scenario: A neuron shows no response to capsaicin, and also no response to the final KCl pulse.
steps.prompt: What do you conclude about it?
options: It's a capsaicin-insensitive but healthy neuron
It was probably unhealthy or dead — exclude it
It's TRPV1+ but desensitized to capsaicin
steps.explanation: KCl should excite any living neuron. No KCl response means the cell was unhealthy — its capsaicin 'no' is uninterpretable, so exclude it.
steps.followUp: That's why KCl (or high-K⁺) goes at the end: it validates the silent cells.

variants.prompt: No capsaicin response AND no KCl response means the neuron is…
variants.explanation: A dead cell can't respond to KCl; its silence isn't informative.

steps.prompt: Why include a KCl pulse at the end at all?
options: As a positive control that the silent neurons are still alive
To pick out which of the neurons are the nociceptors
To reset every neuron to rest before the next trial
To wash the remaining capsaicin back out of the dish
steps.explanation: KCl is the viability check — it separates 'truly unresponsive' from 'dead'.

variants.setup: You want to trust your non-responders.
variants.reveal: KCl confirms the silent neurons could have responded.

reviewNotes: Calcium trace interpretation; KCl positive control.
